Subject: Pricing & batching follow-up — token volumes, $/1M target, concurrency assumptions

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size an accurate estimate: 

Call recap (high level):
- Use case: multi-tenant analytics assistant that answers product & usage questions for end customers (mix of short Q&A + 2–3 paragraph summaries).
- Primary models: preference toward open Llama-family variants or moderate-size finetuned generation models (we discussed 7B–13B equivalent).
- Goal: keep cost predictable while maintaining response quality; avoid overprovisioning.

Pricing & capacity items I want to confirm:
1) Monthly token volume: you mentioned a rough target of 30M–50M tokens/month. Can you confirm a single-number estimate or expected range by month 3?
2) Budget range / target unit economics: you said your finance goal is ~ $/1M tokens target — can you confirm the target number you’d be comfortable with (e.g., $10/1M, $20/1M, etc.)?
3) Workload shape and batching expectations:
   - Is traffic steady throughout the day (continuous, low variance) or spiky with identifiable peak windows?
   - Typical request size (input + generation) and whether you expect many short requests (<=128 tokens) vs. frequent long summaries (>=512 tokens).
   - Target concurrency (average and peak QPS) — rough numbers are fine (e.g., avg 20 QPS, peak 75 QPS).

Next steps I propose after you confirm the above:
- We’ll run a quick hosted cost model showing unit economics at three batching/concurrency assumptions (best-effort batching, continuous batching with 200ms wait, and dedicated-reserved nodes).
- If numbers look good, we can set up a short trial (1–2 weeks) with a fixed token allowance so you can validate quality + real cost.

I attached a one-pager (redwood-pricing-quicklook.pdf) and a lightweight spreadsheet (workload-batching-assumptions.xlsx) that shows how batching and concurrency map to $/1M token estimates — fill in the cells with your best estimates and I’ll produce a tailored quote.

Thanks —
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — appreciated the clear recap. Quick answers below: 

1) Monthly token volume: our current conservative forecast is 35M tokens/month in month 1, scaling to ~55M by month 6 if adoption goes as expected. For the quote please model 40M (base) and 60M (upside).

2) Budget / $/1M target: finance is looking for ~ $15/1M tokens as a target to make the economics work for our pricing tier (we can stretch to $20/1M if the latency SLOs are met).

3) Workload shape and batching:
   - Traffic is fairly continuous with predictable weekday peaks (US business hours). Expect steady baseline with 15–25 QPS average, peaking to ~70 QPS during morning and post-release spikes.
   - Typical request size: 70 tokens input + 180 tokens generation (total ~250 tokens) for the summary flow; short Q&A flows are ~40–80 tokens.
   - We expect mostly single-turn requests (no long multi-turn sessions), but some caching of common prompts is possible.

Let me know if you need more granularity (percentiles on request length / QPS). For quoting, please include: hosted per-token estimate at different batching latencies, and cost for a reserved-dedicated pool option.

—Samir

Hey all — adding a couple of technical sizing notes from our side to make sure the quote aligns with Samir’s workload: 

- Continuous batching behavior: since traffic is steady, our serving runtime will form continuous micro-batches with low wait times; you’ll see batching benefits even with modest concurrency (15–25 QPS). We typically model three batching scenarios for cost estimates:
  1) Minimal batching (near-zero wait) — worst-case for tokens/second but best for tail latency.
  2) Continuous batching (200–300ms batching window) — good tradeoff: reduces GPU cost by ~20–40% depending on model and request size.
  3) Aggressive batching (500ms+) — higher token efficiency, worsened p50/p95 latency.

- For the numbers Samir provided (~250 tokens/request avg):
  - At avg 20 QPS, that’s roughly 20 * 250 * 3600 * 24 * 30 ≈ 1.3B tokens/month — this seems high vs Samir’s 40–60M. I think we need to clarify units: Samir, are your QPS numbers per second of active user queries or per-customer? The 15–25 QPS you mentioned earlier sounds like peak QPS across a small percentage of traffic.

  - If the true monthly volume is 40M tokens, that implies a much lower sustained QPS (e.g., avg ~1.3 QPS with bursts) given the 250-token average. So we should sync on whether Samir’s 15–25 QPS is peak instantaneous concurrency vs sustained.

- Cache & prefix reuse: if many queries are similar we can enable prefix/KV caching which can further reduce effective tokens for repeated prompts; worth instrumenting in the trial.

I’ll draft three cost buckets (hosted) assuming: 40M / 60M tokens and batching windows (0ms, 250ms, 500ms). Marissa — I’ll need a confirmation on avg vs peak QPS to produce the per-QPS/dedicated sizing.

Thanks,
Rishi

Samir / Priya — thanks for the quick clarifications. Couple follow ups and proposed next steps: 

1) QPS clarification: Samir — when you said 15–25 QPS that was describing short peak windows (instantaneous concurrency during high-load minutes) not sustained throughout the day. For modeling I’ll ask Rishi to size sustained baseline at ~1.5 QPS (which aligns with ~40M tokens/month at 250 tokens/request) and peak concurrency at 70 QPS. Rishi — please use sustained avg 1.5 QPS, 95th percentile bursts to 70 QPS for the dedicated/reserved estimate.

2) Unit economics target: confirmed that Finance is targeting ~$15/1M tokens (flex to $20/1M if SLOs met). We’ll model both to show delta.

3) Deliverables I’ll ship next week:
   - Hosted cost model: $/1M tokens and total monthly at 40M and 60M tokens across minimal / continuous (250ms) / aggressive batching.
   - Dedicated sizing estimate: nodes required to meet p95 latency at 70 QPS (with recommended autoscaling/burst config).
   - Suggested trial scope: 2-week hosted trial with a 5M token allowance and instrumentation to measure effective token reduction from caching and batching.

If that all sounds good I’ll schedule a short follow-up next Wednesday to walk through the cost model.

Thanks —
Marissa
